note.note:
ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Burning/stinging pain on urination with increased urinary frequency for just under 1 week; no clear precipitating exposure or allergen.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Began ≈6–7 days ago, gradually persistent; today first noted pink-tinged urine.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No previous similar urinary episodes; no prior ED visits or injection therapy.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Clindamycin – adverse reaction (type/details not documented).  
  • Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (brand/dose not documented); Mebeverine for IBS (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context: 19-year-old university student living in halls with flatmate; long-term boyfriend, sexually active; occasional alcohol, one-time cannabis use.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: None reported/observed.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or respiratory distress reported.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (telephone consultation).
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not applicable (telephone).

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial lower urinary tract infection).
  Evidence: Classic triad of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic ache; micro-hematuria; absence of fever/flank pain.
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with DDx):
  1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – high likelihood; matches symptom pattern.
  2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – medium likelihood; unprotected intercourse, but no discharge or pelvic pain.
  3. Distal ureteric/bladder calculus – low–medium likelihood; hematuria possible, but lacks colicky flank pain.
  (No ENT differentials applicable.)

Plan:
- Diagnostics: Mid-stream urine sample for dipstick and culture; arrange drop-off at practice.
- Pharmacologic therapy: Start short course oral antibiotic (Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim per clinician discussion); ensure adequate hydration; use paracetamol for discomfort.
- Patient instructions:
  • Complete full antibiotic course as prescribed.  
  • Maintain high fluid intake.  
  • Seek urgent care if fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or worsening hematuria occur.
- Follow-up: Clinic will contact with culture results; if no improvement within one week, patient to return for review (possible further evaluation or imaging).
- Preventive/education: Review safe-sex practices and STI screening if symptoms persist or recur; advised against regular cannabis use; routine contraceptive pill continuation.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: No recorded vitals, physical exam, urine dipstick result, or dosage details for current medications; no STI testing arranged despite consideration; auto-injector/allergy action plan not applicable but allergy details limited.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, minimal background noise; no inaudible sections affecting clinical content.
